dbms: Which SQL clause filters rows before grouping?
WHERE filters individual rows before aggregation. HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY.
What normal form eliminates partial dependency on a composite key?
2NF removes partial dependencies where a non-key attribute depends on part of a composite primary key.
Which ACID property ensures all-or-nothing execution?
Atomicity guarantees a transaction completes fully or rolls back with no partial updates.
What structure speeds up SELECT queries on indexed columns?
B+ tree indexes reduce search cost from O(n) scan to O(log n) lookup for selective queries.
In ER modeling, a weak entity depends on what?
Primary key of another weak entity only always
Weak entities use partial keys and identifying relationships with owner entities.
Which join returns matching rows from both tables only?
FULL OUTER always with nulls on both sides for non-match only inner
INNER JOIN outputs rows where join condition matches in both tables.
If X->Y, knowing X value determines Y value in a relation instance.
Two-phase locking (2PL) is used for what?
2PL ensures serializable schedules by growing then shrinking lock sets.
Which key uniquely identifies a row and cannot be NULL?
Primary key enforces uniqueness and NOT NULL for entity identification.
Views are stored queries presenting derived data without mandatory physical copy.
Which anomaly occurs when a deleted row loses associated data unintentionally?
Deletion anomaly happens when removing one fact accidentally removes unrelated facts.
BCNF requires every determinant to be what?
In BCNF, for every non-trivial FD X->Y, X must be a superkey.
Which SQL command removes all rows but keeps table structure?
TRUNCATE deallocates data pages quickly while preserving schema; DELETE removes row-by-row.
What is a foreign key used for?
Foreign keys enforce valid references to parent table primary/unique keys.
Which isolation level prevents dirty reads in SQL standard?
READ COMMITTED avoids reading uncommitted data from other transactions.
Clustered index in SQL Server means what?
Table rows stored in index key order
Clustered index defines physical row ordering; only one per table in SQL Server.
Which aggregate ignores NULL values by default?
SUM always counts null as zero always wrong
COUNT(column) counts non-null entries; COUNT(*) counts rows regardless of nulls.
Spurious tuples after natural join of decomposed relations
Lossless decomposition ensures joining parts yields exactly original relation without extras.
Which operator selects columns in relational algebra?
Projection (pi) chooses attributes; selection (sigma) filters rows.
Write-ahead logging (WAL) supports which ACID property most directly?
WAL ensures committed changes survive crashes by logging before applying to database pages.
Which SQL keyword removes duplicate rows in result?
SELECT DISTINCT eliminates duplicate tuples from query output.
3NF removes transitive dependencies where non-key attributes depend on other non-key attributes.
Which concurrency problem is prevented by serializable isolation?
All anomalies including phantom in theory
Serializable execution is equivalent to some serial order, preventing standard anomalies.
Index includes all columns needed by query
Covering index contains queried columns avoiding key lookup to table data.
Primary key not null and unique
Entity integrity: primary key values unique and not null.
Which join includes all rows from left table and matches from right?
LEFT OUTER JOIN keeps all left rows, filling NULLs when no right match.
Multivalued dependency requires what normal form?
4NF decomposes relations to eliminate non-trivial multivalued dependencies.
Which statement grants privileges in SQL?
GRANT assigns permissions; REVOKE removes them.
OCC validates at commit using timestamps/versions assuming low conflict rate.
Which key can serve as primary key among candidates?
Any candidate key may be chosen as primary; others become alternate keys.
Shadow paging is related to what?
Crash recovery without WAL complexity in simple systems
Shadow paging switches pointers between current and shadow pages for atomic updates.
Which SQL function returns number of rows matching condition in group?
COUNT tallies rows or non-null values within grouped partitions.
Referential integrity on DELETE CASCADE does what?
Deletes child rows when parent deleted
Sets child PK null always invalid
ON DELETE CASCADE propagates parent deletion to dependent child rows.
Which normal form deals with join dependencies beyond 4NF?
5NF (project-join normal form) addresses join dependencies not implied by keys.
Dense index in indexing means what?
Index entry for every search key value in file
Dense index has entries for each record/search key; sparse indexes block headers.
ORDER BY sorts result tuples ascending or descending by specified columns.
Dirty read occurs at which isolation level allowance?
READ UNCOMMITTED permits reading uncommitted changes from other transactions.
Which ER relationship connects three or more entity sets?
Ternary (n-ary) relationships involve more than two participating entity types.
Checkpoint in recovery serves to what?
Reduce redo/undo work by marking consistent state
Checkpoints limit recovery scan by recording dirty pages and log sequence at point.
Which constraint ensures column values are unique but allows one NULL in SQL standard?
UNIQUE allows multiple NULLs in SQL standard unlike PRIMARY KEY.
Star schema is used in what?
Star schema organizes fact table surrounded by dimension tables for analytics.
Which operation combines relations vertically with same schema?
UNION concatenates compatible relations removing duplicates unless UNION ALL.
Release all locks only after commit/abort
Strict two-phase locking holds all locks until transaction ends ensuring recoverability.
Which index type supports range queries well?
Bitmap on high-cardinality only always bad
B+ trees maintain sorted order enabling efficient range scans.
Partial dependency example in relation (A,B)->C with dependency A->C violates?
Non-key attribute depending on part of composite key violates 2NF.
Which SQL command modifies existing rows?
UPDATE changes column values for rows matching WHERE predicate.
Timestamp ordering protocol uses what to order transactions?
Timestamps determine serializability order; conflicting ops checked against timestamps.
Candidate keys are minimal sets of attributes forming a superkey.
HAVING clause differs from WHERE because it filters what?
HAVING applies predicates to grouped results; WHERE filters input rows.
Armstrong axioms are used to infer what?
Armstrong rules (reflexivity, augmentation, transitivity) derive FD closures.
